# Pre-registration: Canopy loss at scale: every rule, with and without cloud correction, on 21 forests

Written before any data was read. The result note cites this note by path and content id; the transparency log orders the two.

## Question

On all 21 forests the lab has scored, pooled, which rules find 2024-25 canopy loss best by MCC, does a sub-pixel green-share rule beat the registry's deforestation_alert_ndvi_drop@1, and does a temporal cloud screen improve each detector?

## Reference (independent of every method)

Hansen Global Forest Change v1.13 loss year and 2000 tree cover (Landsat, 30 m; Hansen et al. 2013), read through emem's forest_raster@1 for the same box. Independent of every method: they read Sentinel-2, the reference reads Landsat.

## Labels

A cell is forest when its mean 2000 tree cover is 30% or more; others are left out. A forest cell is LOSS when 5% or more of its pixels lost cover in 2024 or 2025, and STABLE when none did and none lost cover in 2023 (a 2023 clearing first seen in January 2024 is neither). Cells in between are left out and counted.

## Methods

- `registry:deforestation_alert_ndvi_drop@1` (registry; emem algorithm registry: Hansen et al. 2013; GLAD-S2 alert documentation). The registry formula: alert when NDVI fell more than 0.20 from about 60 days before (the nearest pass 40 to 80 days earlier) and now reads under 0.5. Source blake3 `37af18ffa76ee1c75b9f1308daef65eb96d7b6029c20cd8418e7438f02588af8`.
- `registry:burn_severity_from_dnbr@1` (registry; emem algorithm registry: Key & Benson 2006). The registry formula on consecutive clear passes: dNBR (before minus after) of 0.27 or more, moderate-low severity or worse. Source blake3 `2fc52f4de53b5c1c3fcf0dbc251076e8a0dc8990c2e68f88865e604bc4186645`.
- `desk:vegetation_loss@1` (desk; emem arcade forest desk (agents/measures.py new_bare_ground)). What the forest desk runs: NDVI 0.25 below the previous clear pass, from at least 0.4, and still at least 0.125 down on the next two passes. Source blake3 `f4eb179b417a2243b5d4017b0351fc711a4978e17c9257fb694c7792d70f0096`.
- `desk:vegetation_loss_nbr@1` (desk; emem arcade forest desk, fire places (Key & Benson 2006 threshold)). The desk rule on NBR: 0.27 below the previous pass, from at least 0.3, held two passes. Source blake3 `c069124153b74f681343cc7382c7b0a36c513a04ccf804716b3895f87ab2bbb3`.
- `lab:seasonal_loss_ndvi@1` (lab; proposed by the emem methods lab (this experiment)). NDVI after t (median of 45 days) at least 0.20 below both the median of the 90 days before t and the median of the same 45 days a year earlier, from at least 0.4. Source blake3 `4e0f3a20fa918963aa68657d0f44c820f41c9bdadfe6b84ae69b004007aabbff`.
- `lab:seasonal_loss_nbr@1` (lab; proposed by the emem methods lab (this experiment)). The same rule on NBR, with the 0.27 drop of moderate burn severity, from at least 0.3. Source blake3 `0202d215169f7be53b2afaee3edb9143174f625cbea5417801a5396b18d869a8`.
- `lab:seasonal_loss_either@1` (lab; proposed by the emem methods lab (this experiment)). Either seasonal rule: clearing shows first in NDVI, burning first in NBR. Source blake3 `2a1d57542e35bb5e648f54ef0990ad6ba0c655398ce5cac45e024e84f80a8b89`.
- `lab:subcell_loss_p10@1` (lab; proposed by the emem methods lab after the replication failed (2026-10-29)). The seasonal rule on the cell's darkest tenth of pixels (its NDVI 10th percentile) instead of its median: a clearing over a fifth of a 400 m cell barely moves the median and drags the 10th percentile down. Loss when that percentile, over the 45 days from t, sits 0.20 below both its own 90 days before and the same 45 days a year earlier, from at least 0.3. Source blake3 `4c36e36a1ce7ddbcdb6fc7eaa5808f853024f3e49d2f3079954760d869311a6c`.
- `lab:green_fraction_loss@1` (lab; proposed by the emem methods lab: sub-pixel canopy share (2026-10-29)). Sub-pixel loss: the share of the cell's pixels above NDVI 0.4, read from its percentiles, falls by 0.15 (15% of the cell) below both its own 90 days before and the same 45 days a year earlier, from at least 70% green. It counts cleared area rather than waiting for a clearing to move the cell's median. Source blake3 `7166559c46f08c73143f6f34ee4e83266caf54f321452d557e61acadecd84470`.
- `registry:deforestation_alert_ndvi_drop@1+screen` (lab; emem methods lab: Chen et al. 2004 screen before registry:deforestation_alert_ndvi_drop@1). The temporal cloud screen applied to every input series, then registry:deforestation_alert_ndvi_drop@1. Source blake3 `7dc76b08da1dda6bbbbc76793d63859c8f66e9c72f035f05c5591a2d6cab8696`.
- `registry:burn_severity_from_dnbr@1+screen` (lab; emem methods lab: Chen et al. 2004 screen before registry:burn_severity_from_dnbr@1). The temporal cloud screen applied to every input series, then registry:burn_severity_from_dnbr@1. Source blake3 `ff2e5fc88b08baada91a481ed5556d60441a1ed273f2cbe209bc5bf96c77fbaf`.
- `desk:vegetation_loss@1+screen` (lab; emem methods lab: Chen et al. 2004 screen before desk:vegetation_loss@1). The temporal cloud screen applied to every input series, then desk:vegetation_loss@1. Source blake3 `e6519069bc124fe6b1adc75b917f721ab554be7aecfbfa13730190993f6a7af5`.
- `lab:subcell_loss_p10@1+screen` (lab; emem methods lab: Chen et al. 2004 screen before lab:subcell_loss_p10@1). The temporal cloud screen applied to every input series, then lab:subcell_loss_p10@1. Source blake3 `ab899342bd017f1342434023e9db256365f347719078bbea59597688de3c0409`.
- `lab:green_fraction_loss@1+screen` (lab; emem methods lab: Chen et al. 2004 screen before lab:green_fraction_loss@1). The temporal cloud screen applied to every input series, then lab:green_fraction_loss@1. Source blake3 `33b3337641d2b9ea105e27b59ce52d2d8c87046bd8247ceebe891d666bf6338a`.

## The search

Besides the fixed methods, the lab searches 32 variants of its seasonal rule (index NDVI or NBR; drop 0.15, 0.20, 0.25 or 0.30; starting level 0.3 or 0.4; post window 30 or 45 days; rule source blake3 `16256593f0e0cb61f7632fa6716284c95fb45e688a36bf7c626e9e36565c6e56`). The pick is scored by leave-one-site-out cross-validation: for each site, the variant with the best F1 on the other sites is chosen and applied to it, so every scored cell comes from a site its rule never saw. The searched rule beats the baseline when the 95% paired-bootstrap interval of its out-of-sample F1 minus the baseline's lies wholly above zero. The variant best on all sites is the one proposed, with the cross-validated score as its expected performance.

## Raw-data enhancement under test

The temporal cloud screen (drop a pass more than 0.1 below both neighbours; Chen et al. 2004) is applied before 5 detectors. For each, the screened and unscreened versions are compared on the same cells by the paired bootstrap of the deciding score: the screen helps a detector when the 95% interval of the difference lies wholly above zero, and hurts it when wholly below.

## Metric and decision rule

Each method flags a cell when it sees loss with a date from 2024-01-01 to 2026-03-31 (the reference is annual, so a loss seen early in 2026 can be 2025's). Scored over LOSS and STABLE forest cells pooled across sites: Matthews correlation (MCC), with F1, precision, recall and false-alarm rate beside it. MCC decides because it counts the stable forest a method left alone: on 29 October 2026 the F1 rule let a detector that flagged 74% of stable forest win where loss was common. A method beats the registry baseline `registry:deforestation_alert_ndvi_drop@1` when the 95% paired-bootstrap interval (2,000 resamples of cells, seed 7) of its MCC minus the baseline's lies wholly above zero.

## Sites

- Amazon frontier, Rondonia (-9.729, -63.030), a box 4.8 km a side
- Sao Felix do Xingu, Para (-6.640, -51.990), a box 4.8 km a side
- Chiquitania, Santa Cruz, Bolivia (-16.300, -61.500), a box 4.8 km a side
- Central Kalimantan peat forest (-2.300, 113.900), a box 4.8 km a side
- Jasper, Alberta (52.870, -118.080), a box 4.8 km a side
- Prey Lang, Cambodia (13.200, 105.400), a box 4.8 km a side
- Ituri rainforest, Congo basin (1.400, 28.600), a box 4.8 km a side
- Madre de Dios, Peru (-12.600, -70.100), a box 4.8 km a side
- Sinop, Mato Grosso (-11.900, -55.300), a box 4.8 km a side
- Gran Chaco, Paraguay (-21.500, -60.600), a box 4.8 km a side
- Riau, Sumatra (0.600, 101.900), a box 4.8 km a side
- Tanintharyi, Myanmar (12.300, 99.000), a box 4.8 km a side
- Tai forest edge, Cote d'Ivoire (5.900, -7.200), a box 4.8 km a side
- Western Ghats, Karnataka (13.900, 75.300), a box 4.8 km a side
- Guaviare, Colombia (2.300, -72.600), a box 4.8 km a side
- Ucayali, Peru (-8.400, -74.600), a box 4.8 km a side
- Merauke, Papua (-7.900, 140.400), a box 4.8 km a side
- Menabe, Madagascar (-20.000, 44.600), a box 4.8 km a side

- Acre, Brazil (-9.900, -67.600), a box 4.8 km a side
